anonymous_statement.{u_1}
  {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E]
  [BorelSpace E] (S : Finset ℕ) (c : ℕ → ℝ) (w z : E) (hw : ‖w‖ = 1) (hz : ‖z‖ = 1) :
  Inner.inner ℝ
      (anonymous_object_2 S c w)
      (anonymous_object_2 S c z) =
    ∑ j ∈ S, ↑j.factorial * c j ^ 2 * Inner.inner ℝ w z ^ j

blind_reconstruction.text: Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its induced norm and Borel sigma-algebra. Let gamma_E be the centered Gaussian probability measure on E with covariance the identity. Let L^2(gamma_E; R) be the real Hilbert space of square-integrable real-valued functions modulo gamma_E-almost-everywhere equality. Write H_j for the unnormalized probabilists' Hermite polynomial of degree j, with its integer coefficients interpreted in R (H_0(t)=1, H_1(t)=t, and H_(n+1)(t)=t H_n(t)-n H_(n-1)(t) for n>=1). Define Phi_j(w)=[x |-> H_j(<w,x>)] in L^2(gamma_E; R), where brackets denote the almost-everywhere equivalence class of the literal square-integrable function displayed. For every finite subset S of N={0,1,2,...}, every coefficient sequence c:N -> R, and every pair w,z in E satisfying ||w||=1 and ||z||=1, define F_(S,c)(v)=sum_(j in S) c(j) Phi_j(v) for v in E. Then the real Hilbert-space inner product satisfies <F_(S,c)(w),F_(S,c)(z)>_(L^2(gamma_E;R)) = sum_(j in S) j! c(j)^2 <w,z>^j. The factorial is interpreted as a real number. The same finite set and same real coefficients occur in both features. Equivalently, the left side is the Gaussian integral of the product of the two displayed finite Hermite sums. This is an exact scalar equality for all such unit w,z, including an empty S and indices j=0.
